summary: This is a University of Melbourne Handbook page for the graduate coursework subject Radical Chemistry (CHEM90054), worth 6.25 points and not available in 2022. The subject outlines the fundamental steps of radical chemistry and shows how these principles apply to synthesizing important molecular frameworks. Its listed intended learning outcomes cover radical stability and reactivity, radical reaction mechanisms, organic photochemistry, and generic analytical and problem-solving skills.
one_line: University of Melbourne graduate subject CHEM90054 on radical chemistry, covering radical stability, reactions, mechanisms and organic photochemistry.
key_facts: Radical Chemistry (CHEM90054) is a graduate coursework subject at The University of Melbourne Handbook.
The subject is not available in 2022.
The page is the 2022 Handbook version of the subject.
The subject outlines the fundamental steps important to radical chemistry.
The subject shows how radical chemistry principles can be used in the synthesis of important molecular frameworks.
Students should be able to understand the factors responsible for radical stability and reactivity.
Students should be able to demonstrate an understanding of important radical reactions and their mechanisms.
Students should be able to demonstrate an understanding of fundamental aspects of organic photochemistry.
Students should be able to use conceptual models to rationalize experimental observations.
Generic skills listed include advanced problem-solving and critical thinking skills.
Generic skills listed include an ability to evaluate the professional literature and a capacity to apply concepts developed in one area to a different context.
Subjects taught in 2022 were delivered in one of three modes: Dual-Delivery, Online or On Campus.
The page was last updated on 12 November 2022.
